You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 5c396185752434b7f7b687e8c86c73ea888337b2 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jan Kandziora <jjj@gmx.de>
Date: Sun, 16 Jul 2017 20:49:04 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] fixed a problem with gcc<7.1 and clang introduced by commit
 c44db863a324bff4608639981ca05f73b43ab275

---
 module/owlib/src/c/ow_server_message.c | 1 +
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)

diff --git a/module/owlib/src/c/ow_server_message.c b/module/owlib/src/c/ow_server_message.c
index 0e04763a..346d0b60 100644
--- a/module/owlib/src/c/ow_server_message.c
+++ b/module/owlib/src/c/ow_server_message.c
@@ -582,6 +582,7 @@ static GOOD_OR_BAD To_Server( struct server_connection_state * scs, struct serve
 			__attribute__ ((fallthrough));
 		case -2:
 			// fnctl error, fall through again
+			;
 			__attribute__ ((fallthrough));
 		case 0:
 			LEVEL_DEBUG("Server connection was closed.  Reconnecting.");
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by a compatibility issue with GCC versions earlier than 7.1 and Clang, which did not properly handle the fallthrough attribute in switch-case statements. The addition of a semicolon (`;`) before the `__attribute__ ((fallthrough));` directive resolved this issue by ensuring that the compiler correctly interpreted the fallthrough behavior in the case statement, preventing potential miscompilation or warnings.

    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    
    Provide a response strictly in the following format:
    Code statements:
    <text1>
    <text2>

    <text4>
    ...
    <textN>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by a compatibility issue with GCC versions earlier than 7.1 and Clang, which did not properly handle the fallthrough attribute in switch-case statements. The addition of a semicolon (`;`) before the `__attribute__ ((fallthrough));` directive resolved this issue by ensuring that the compiler correctly interpreted the fallthrough behavior in the case statement, preventing potential miscompilation or warnings.
